blocks.text: iOS 8 expanded everyday communication and media workflows with richer Messages, deeper Photos editing, new Camera modes, predictive and third-party keyboards, Family Sharing, iCloud Drive, and the Health app.

citations.locator: iOS 8 — Messages, Photos, Camera, QuickType, Health, Family Sharing, and iCloud Drive
Messages; Photos; QuickType; Health; Family Sharing; iCloud Drive

blocks.text: The release also linked iPhone, iPad, and Mac through Continuity, opened new extension and authentication capabilities to developers, and shipped a broad security repair set covering protected data, Safari, Wi-Fi privacy, and lower-level system components.

citations.locator: iOS 8 — Continuity, enterprise features, and accessibility
September 17 public availability and launch features

blocks.text: Apple’s retired support article documents that iOS 8.0.1 caused some iPhone 6 and iPhone 6 Plus devices to lose cellular service and Touch ID functionality.

Apple’s current cumulative iOS 8 notes and archived 2014 security index do not contain an iOS 8.0.1 entry, so this article records only that confirmed regression and does not reconstruct the update’s intended fixes from secondary accounts.
Apple’s preserved support article says iOS 8.0.2 restored cellular service and Touch ID for affected iPhone 6 and iPhone 6 Plus devices that had installed iOS 8.0.1.

The same article says the release carried forward improvements and bug fixes from 8.0.1, but neither Apple’s current cumulative iOS 8 page nor its 2014 security index preserves an itemized 8.0.2 section. This entry therefore does not invent a broader patch list.
iOS 8.1 introduced Apple Pay on supported U.S. devices, added the iCloud Photo Library beta and restored Camera Roll, and extended iPhone SMS and MMS messaging to iPad and Mac.

citations.locator: iOS 8.1 — Apple Pay, Photos, and Messages

blocks.text: The update also repaired Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, rotation, Safari video, messaging, accessibility, and caching-server behavior while addressing published Bluetooth, iCloud, keyboard, and transport-security defects.
iOS 8.1.1 was a maintenance release focused on bug fixes, stability, and performance improvements for iPad 2 and iPhone 4s.

Its security bulletin documents repairs involving private-browsing cache clearing, code validation, lock-screen restrictions, Spotlight location disclosure, sandbox permissions, and WebKit memory handling.
iOS 8.1.2 was a narrow maintenance update whose only itemized consumer change restored access to purchased iTunes Store ringtones that had disappeared from a device.
Apple’s security bulletin says 8.1.2 includes the security content of 8.1.1 rather than documenting a new security delta, so no inherited vulnerability repair is duplicated as an 8.1.2 change.

iOS 8.1.3 reduced the storage needed for software updates and fixed Apple ID password entry, Spotlight app results, and iPad multitasking gestures, while adding controls for standardized testing in education.
The security update tightened protected filesystem paths, executable and kernel validation, enterprise-app installation, trust prompts, and WebKit handling.

iOS 8.2 added the Apple Watch companion app and paired-device Activity view on iPhone 5 and later, while expanding Health units, workout visualization, privacy controls, and large-dataset reliability.

The release also improved stability, hearing-aid connectivity, media and calendar behavior, and Exchange interoperability, and its security bulletin covers telephony, iCloud Keychain, system privilege, activation, and TLS weaknesses.

citations.locator: iOS 8.2 — stability enhancements and bug fixes

blocks.text: iOS 8.3 paired broad performance work with extensive Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, rotation, Messages, Family Sharing, CarPlay, enterprise, and accessibility repairs.

It also redesigned the emoji keyboard, moved iCloud Photo Library out of beta, expanded Siri and Dictation languages, refined Apple Pay and Maps, and shipped a large security update spanning passcode checks, backups, networking, app snapshots, WebKit, and Wi-Fi trust.

citations.locator: iOS 8.3 — other improvements and bug fixes

blocks.text: iOS 8.4 introduced Apple Music inside a redesigned Music app, bringing subscription streaming, personalized recommendations, Beats 1 and curated radio, Connect, and a unified library and playback interface.

citations.locator: Apple Music, Radio, Connect, and June 30 availability

blocks.text: The release also brought audiobook playback and library improvements to iBooks, corrected a Unicode-triggered reboot and accessory issues, and delivered security fixes across app installation, TLS, Mail, Safari, telephony, WebKit, and Wi-Fi.

iOS 8.4.1 concentrated its visible changes on Apple Music, repairing iCloud Music Library activation, offline-only visibility, playlist creation, album artwork, Connect posting, and the Love control in Beats 1.

Its security bulletin documents additional protections for filesystem paths, Wi-Fi history, certificate prompts, CloudKit account state, managed preferences, code signing, media and image parsing, the kernel, Safari, and WebKit.

events.summary: The public iOS 8 release introduced major communication, media, keyboard, health, family, cloud, cross-device, developer-platform, privacy, and security changes.

citations.locator: September 17 public availability and launch features

changes.title: Richer Messages conversations
changes.canonicalSummary: Messages added quick audio, video, and photo sharing plus expanded controls for group conversations.
changes.summary: Users could send voice, video, or photos with a swipe, manage participants and names in group threads, mute a conversation, leave it, share location, and browse attachments from a details view.

changes.title: Photos editing, search, and extensions
changes.canonicalSummary: Photos gained smart adjustments, granular controls, search, new albums, and third-party editing extensions.
changes.summary: The Photos app added one-swipe light and color correction, detailed exposure controls, date and location search, media-specific albums, and direct use of compatible third-party filters and editing tools.

changes.title: Expanded Camera capture tools
changes.canonicalSummary: Camera added time-lapse recording, a capture timer, direct exposure adjustment, and hardware-specific modes.
changes.summary: Camera introduced time-lapse and a timer, let users adjust exposure before capture, and extended burst or panorama options to the documented supported devices.

changes.title: QuickType and third-party keyboards
changes.canonicalSummary: The system introduced context-aware predictive typing and support for third-party keyboards.
changes.summary: QuickType offered on-device predictions tailored to writing context and supported languages, while a new extension point allowed compatible third-party keyboards to work system-wide.

changes.title: Health app and HealthKit
changes.canonicalSummary: A new Health app organized health and fitness data while HealthKit enabled permission-based data exchange between apps.
changes.summary: Health provided a dashboard and optional lock-screen Medical ID, and HealthKit let users authorize compatible health and fitness apps to read or share selected data.

changes.title: Family Sharing
changes.canonicalSummary: Family Sharing connected up to six accounts for eligible purchases, shared collections, locations, and parental approval.
changes.summary: Families could share qualifying store purchases, a photo stream, calendar, and locations while retaining separate Apple IDs and using Ask to Buy for children.

changes.title: iCloud Drive
changes.canonicalSummary: iCloud Drive provided document storage and synchronized access across compatible apps and devices.
changes.summary: Users could store documents in iCloud, work with the same file from compatible applications, and have edits update across supported Apple and Windows devices.

changes.title: Continuity across iOS and Mac
changes.canonicalSummary: Continuity added Handoff, cross-device calls and messaging, Instant Hotspot, and Yosemite-compatible AirDrop.
changes.summary: Supported devices could move an activity between iOS and Mac, use an iPhone connection as an automatic hotspot, handle iPhone calls and messages on other devices, and exchange files with OS X Yosemite.

changes.title: Expanded developer platform
changes.canonicalSummary: The iOS 8 SDK added app extensions, Touch ID APIs, Metal, CloudKit, and new HealthKit and HomeKit frameworks.
changes.summary: Developers gained system extension points, application authentication with Touch ID, a lower-overhead graphics technology, a managed cloud backend, and frameworks for health data and connected-home accessories.

changes.title: Randomized passive Wi-Fi scanning
changes.canonicalSummary: Passive Wi-Fi scans stopped exposing one stable hardware address that could be used to track a device.
changes.summary: Apple addressed device tracking through passive Wi-Fi scans by randomizing the MAC address used during that discovery activity.

events.summary: The surviving first-party record for iOS 8.0.1 documents a cellular-service and Touch ID regression on some iPhone 6 and iPhone 6 Plus devices; no itemized Apple patch list survives.

changes.title: iPhone 6 cellular and Touch ID regression
changes.canonicalSummary: The update could disable cellular service and Touch ID on affected iPhone 6 and iPhone 6 Plus devices.
changes.summary: Apple documented loss of cellular connectivity and Touch ID after some iPhone 6 and iPhone 6 Plus devices installed iOS 8.0.1.

events.summary: The public iOS 8.0.2 release repaired the iPhone 6 and iPhone 6 Plus cellular-service and Touch ID regression from 8.0.1 and carried forward unspecified earlier fixes.

changes.title: Restored iPhone 6 cellular service and Touch ID
changes.canonicalSummary: The update restored cellular connectivity and Touch ID for devices affected by the iOS 8.0.1 regression.
changes.summary: Apple says iOS 8.0.2 fixed the loss of cellular service and Touch ID that could follow installation of iOS 8.0.1 on iPhone 6 or iPhone 6 Plus.

events.summary: The public iOS 8.1 release added Apple Pay, expanded Photos and cross-device messaging, repaired connectivity and accessibility problems, and delivered targeted security protections.

changes.title: Apple Pay launch in the United States
changes.canonicalSummary: Apple Pay became available in the United States on supported iPhone and iPad hardware.
changes.summary: iOS 8.1 enabled Apple Pay for in-store purchases on iPhone 6 and iPhone 6 Plus and for supported in-app purchases on the documented devices, initially in the United States.

changes.title: iCloud Photo Library beta and Camera Roll
changes.canonicalSummary: Photos added the iCloud Photo Library beta, restored Camera Roll, and warned before low-storage time-lapse capture.
changes.summary: The Photos app introduced iCloud Photo Library as a beta service, displayed Camera Roll and My Photo Stream in the documented configurations, and added a low-space warning for time-lapse video.

changes.title: SMS and MMS relay to iPad and Mac
changes.canonicalSummary: An iPhone could relay carrier SMS and MMS conversations through a user’s iPad and Mac.
changes.summary: iPhone users gained the ability to send and receive SMS and MMS messages from their iPad and Mac as part of the cross-device messaging experience.

changes.title: Connectivity, rotation, and Safari video fixes
changes.canonicalSummary: The release repaired documented Wi-Fi, hands-free Bluetooth, screen rotation, and Safari video failures.
changes.summary: Apple addressed Wi-Fi performance with some base stations, Bluetooth hands-free connection failures, stalled rotation, and Safari videos that sometimes would not play.

changes.title: New network, AirDrop, Dictation, and HealthKit controls
changes.canonicalSummary: Users gained cellular-network selection, Passbook AirDrop, independent Dictation control, and background HealthKit access.
changes.summary: The update added an operator-dependent 2G, 3G, or LTE selector, AirDrop for Passbook passes, a Dictation setting separate from Siri, and background HealthKit data access for compatible apps.

changes.title: Accessibility and Caching Server reliability
changes.canonicalSummary: Guided Access, VoiceOver, hearing aids, Braille input, and OS X Caching Server received targeted fixes.
changes.summary: Apple repaired Guided Access, third-party keyboard use with VoiceOver, hearing-aid stability and audio, tone dialing, several VoiceOver input paths, and delivery of iOS updates through OS X Caching Server.

changes.title: QuickType credential-learning restriction
changes.canonicalSummary: QuickType stopped learning from fields whose autocomplete settings indicated that credentials should not be retained.
changes.summary: Apple addressed CVE-2014-4450 by reapplying input-field criteria during element changes and excluding fields with autocomplete disabled from QuickType learning.

changes.title: SSL 3.0 CBC downgrade protection
changes.canonicalSummary: Secure Transport disabled CBC cipher suites after failed modern TLS attempts to limit the documented SSL 3.0 downgrade attack.
changes.summary: Apple addressed CVE-2014-3566 by preventing a connection fallback sequence from retaining affected CBC suites when an attacker blocked newer TLS attempts.

events.summary: The public iOS 8.1.1 release improved older-device performance and stability while correcting private-browsing, lock-screen, Spotlight-location, and other documented security weaknesses.

changes.title: iPad 2 and iPhone 4s performance improvements
changes.canonicalSummary: The maintenance update targeted stability and performance on iPad 2 and iPhone 4s.
changes.summary: Apple described iOS 8.1.1 as including bug fixes and increased stability, with performance improvements specifically for iPad 2 and iPhone 4s.

changes.title: Private-browsing cache clearing
changes.canonicalSummary: Leaving private browsing reliably cleared the affected cached website data.
changes.summary: Apple addressed CVE-2014-4460 by changing caching behavior so website data did not remain in the affected cache after private browsing ended.

changes.title: Lock-screen passcode-attempt enforcement
changes.canonicalSummary: The lock screen consistently enforced the configured limit on failed passcode attempts.
changes.summary: Apple addressed CVE-2014-4451 by adding enforcement for circumstances in which an attacker holding the device could exceed the failed-passcode-attempt limit.

changes.title: Spotlight initial-location minimization
changes.canonicalSummary: Spotlight and Safari stopped sending approximate location before the user entered a suggestions query.
changes.summary: Apple addressed CVE-2014-4453 by removing approximate location from the initial Spotlight Suggestions connection and sending it only with a user query.

events.summary: The public iOS 8.1.2 release was a narrow maintenance update that addressed purchased iTunes Store ringtones disappearing from a device.

changes.title: Purchased ringtone restoration
changes.canonicalSummary: Purchased iTunes Store ringtones that had disappeared from a device could be restored.
changes.summary: Apple addressed a problem that could remove purchased iTunes Store ringtones and supplied a device-based restoration path for affected purchases.

events.summary: The public iOS 8.1.3 release reduced update-storage requirements, repaired account, search, and iPad gesture problems, added education controls, and strengthened platform security.

changes.title: Lower software-update storage requirement
changes.canonicalSummary: Installing a software update required less free storage on the device.
changes.summary: Apple reduced the amount of device storage needed to perform an iOS software update.

changes.title: Messages and FaceTime Apple ID sign-in fix
changes.canonicalSummary: Affected users could enter their Apple ID password for Messages and FaceTime.
changes.summary: The release corrected a condition that prevented some users from entering an Apple ID password in Messages and FaceTime.

changes.title: Spotlight app results and iPad gesture fixes
changes.canonicalSummary: Spotlight resumed showing app results and iPad multitasking gestures resumed working.
changes.summary: Apple repaired two separate user-interface failures: missing application results in Spotlight and nonfunctional multitasking gestures on iPad.

changes.title: Education standardized-testing controls
changes.canonicalSummary: New configuration options supported standardized testing deployments in education.
changes.summary: The update added device-configuration options intended for education standardized-testing environments.

changes.title: AppleFileConduit path validation
changes.canonicalSummary: Additional path checks prevented crafted afc commands from reaching protected filesystem areas.
changes.summary: Apple addressed CVE-2014-4480 by adding checks around symbolic links handled through AppleFileConduit.

changes.title: Enterprise app-container protection
changes.canonicalSummary: Enterprise-signed apps were prevented from taking over another installed app’s local container in affected scenarios.
changes.summary: Apple addressed CVE-2014-4493 by changing installation rules so an enterprise application could not override an existing application in the documented cases.

events.summary: The public iOS 8.2 release prepared iPhone for Apple Watch, expanded Health, improved system and accessory reliability, repaired media and calendar workflows, and closed documented security flaws.

changes.title: Apple Watch companion and Activity apps
changes.canonicalSummary: Supported iPhones gained Apple Watch pairing and settings plus an Activity view for paired fitness data.
changes.summary: On iPhone 5 and later, a new Apple Watch app handled pairing, synchronization, and settings, while Activity appeared after pairing to display fitness data and achievements.

changes.title: Expanded Health controls and workouts
changes.canonicalSummary: Health added unit selection, third-party workout sessions, motion-tracking privacy control, and several data fixes.
changes.summary: Users could choose units for several health metrics, add and visualize workouts from compatible apps, disable tracked motion categories, and benefit from fixes for large datasets, Medical ID, sources, graphs, and nutrient units.

changes.title: App stability and hearing-aid connectivity
changes.canonicalSummary: Mail, Maps Flyover, Music, VoiceOver, and Made for iPhone hearing-aid connectivity received reliability improvements.
changes.summary: Apple reported stability work for Mail, Flyover, Music, and VoiceOver together with improved connectivity for Made for iPhone hearing aids.

changes.title: Media, restore, and sync fixes
changes.canonicalSummary: The release repaired favorite navigation, iCloud restore, music sync, and deleted-audiobook behavior.
changes.summary: Apple corrected navigation to some Maps favorites, duplicate-purchase interference with iCloud restore, music or playlist sync from iTunes, and audiobooks that remained after deletion.

citations.locator: iOS 8.2 — media and restore bug fixes

changes.title: Car and Bluetooth call-audio fixes
changes.canonicalSummary: Call audio routed correctly through car speakers and was audible at the intended point in Bluetooth calls.
changes.summary: The update addressed Siri Eyes Free call audio not reaching car speakers and a Bluetooth calling path that stayed silent until a call was answered.

changes.title: Calendar and Exchange reliability
changes.canonicalSummary: Calendar time zones, recurring meetings, gateways, organizer notes, and accepted-event availability received fixes.
changes.summary: Apple repaired GMT event display, missing instances in custom recurring Exchange meetings, gateway certificate setup, overwritten organizer notes, and accepted events that did not automatically show as busy.

changes.title: Class 0 SMS restart protection
changes.canonicalSummary: Improved message validation prevented a crafted Class 0 SMS from triggering the documented device restart.
changes.summary: Apple addressed CVE-2015-1063 by correcting a null-pointer path in CoreTelephony’s handling of Class 0 SMS messages.

changes.title: FREAK TLS downgrade protection
changes.canonicalSummary: Secure Transport stopped accepting short ephemeral RSA keys in the documented full-strength connection scenario.
changes.summary: Apple addressed CVE-2015-1067, known as FREAK, by removing support for the affected ephemeral RSA key behavior.

events.summary: The public iOS 8.3 release delivered broad performance and reliability work, a redesigned emoji keyboard, expanded cloud and language features, and a substantial set of security corrections.

changes.title: Broad system performance improvements
changes.canonicalSummary: App launch, responsiveness, Messages, Wi-Fi, Control Center, Safari tabs, and keyboard paths were tuned for performance.
changes.summary: Apple reported performance improvements across launching and interacting with apps, Messages, Wi-Fi, Control Center, Safari tabs, third-party keyboards, shortcuts, and Simplified Chinese input.

changes.title: Wi-Fi and Bluetooth reliability
changes.canonicalSummary: The update repaired repeated credential prompts, Wi-Fi disconnects, hands-free call drops, and speaker playback failures.
changes.summary: Apple addressed continuous login prompts, intermittent Wi-Fi disconnections, hands-free calls that disconnected, and audio that stopped with some Bluetooth speakers.

changes.title: Orientation and rotation reliability
changes.canonicalSummary: Portrait recovery, rotation stability, device orientation, and post-multitasking layout received fixes.
changes.summary: The release repaired failures to return to portrait, instability while rotating, upside-down iPhone 6 Plus orientation, and apps that retained the wrong orientation after multitasking.

changes.title: Messages reliability and sender filtering
changes.canonicalSummary: Messages repaired group and item controls while adding junk reporting and filtering for unknown iMessage senders.
changes.summary: Apple addressed split group threads, forwarding and deletion controls, and photo previews, and added direct junk reporting plus a filter for iMessages from outside Contacts.

changes.title: Family Sharing and CarPlay fixes
changes.canonicalSummary: Family app access and Ask to Buy improved while CarPlay received display, rotation, and keyboard fixes.
changes.summary: The update repaired family-member app launch, update, and free-download problems, improved Ask to Buy notifications, and fixed black Maps screens, rotated interfaces, and misplaced keyboards in CarPlay.

citations.locator: iOS 8.3 — Family Sharing and CarPlay fixes

changes.title: Enterprise and accessibility reliability
changes.canonicalSummary: Enterprise deployment, Exchange and proxy workflows, VoiceOver, Braille, and Speak Screen received targeted corrections.
changes.summary: Apple documented enterprise installation, calendar, web clip, proxy, Exchange, VPN, Wi-Fi login, and meeting-note fixes alongside VoiceOver, Braille, Home Screen, and Speak Screen repairs.

changes.title: Redesigned emoji keyboard
changes.canonicalSummary: A redesigned emoji keyboard added more than 300 characters.
changes.summary: iOS 8.3 replaced the emoji picker with a redesigned keyboard and expanded the available set by more than 300 characters.

changes.title: iCloud Photo Library and language expansion
changes.canonicalSummary: iCloud Photo Library left beta and Siri and Dictation added documented languages and locales.
changes.summary: Apple optimized iCloud Photo Library for the OS X 10.10.3 Photos app and removed its beta label, while adding the listed Siri regions and new Arabic and Hebrew Dictation options.

citations.locator: iOS 8.3 — iCloud Photo Library, Siri, and Dictation

changes.title: Passcode-guessing interface restriction
changes.canonicalSummary: Entitlement checks blocked unauthorized applications from using the affected passcode-confirmation interface.
changes.summary: Apple addressed CVE-2015-1085 by limiting access to an interface that could otherwise let a malicious application test guesses against the user’s passcode.

changes.title: Task Switcher snapshot redaction
changes.canonicalSummary: Sensitive application snapshots were correctly blurred when displayed in the Task Switcher.
changes.summary: Apple addressed CVE-2015-1116 by correcting UIKit’s handling of snapshots that could expose sensitive app content in the Task Switcher.

events.summary: The public iOS 8.4 release launched Apple Music and its redesigned player, expanded iBooks and audiobooks, repaired visible system defects, and delivered a large security update.

changes.title: Apple Music catalog and recommendations
changes.canonicalSummary: Apple Music combined subscription streaming, offline saving, editorial discovery, and personalized recommendations.
changes.summary: Members could stream or save catalog music, browse editorially selected new releases, and receive personalized playlist and album recommendations in For You.

changes.title: Beats 1 and redesigned radio
changes.canonicalSummary: A live global Beats 1 station joined curated and artist-based Apple Music radio.
changes.summary: Radio added the worldwide live Beats 1 station, expert-programmed stations, and the ability to create a station from an artist or song.

changes.title: Apple Music Connect
changes.canonicalSummary: Connect created an in-app channel for artists to share media and interact with fans.
changes.summary: Artists could publish thoughts, photos, music, and video to followers, while fans could react, comment, and share supported posts.

changes.title: Redesigned Music player and library
changes.canonicalSummary: The Music app unified purchases, subscription content, and playlists with a redesigned player and queue.
changes.summary: My Music brought purchases, Apple Music additions, and playlists together, while the redesigned player added Recently Added, MiniPlayer, and Up Next.

citations.locator: iOS 8.4 — My Music and redesigned music player

changes.title: iBooks audiobooks and library improvements
changes.canonicalSummary: iBooks added in-app audiobook discovery and playback plus new series, font, theme, and accessibility behavior.
changes.summary: Users could browse, download, and play audiobooks inside iBooks, use a dedicated Now Playing view, manage series and preorders, and benefit from documented layout, font, theme, purchase, and iCloud fixes.

changes.title: Unicode, GPS accessory, and Watch app fixes
changes.canonicalSummary: The update repaired a Unicode-triggered reboot, missing GPS accessory data, and deleted Watch apps that reinstalled.
changes.summary: Apple corrected three itemized system defects involving a specific Unicode sequence, location information from GPS accessories, and removed Apple Watch apps returning unexpectedly.

citations.locator: iOS 8.4 — other improvements and bug fixes

changes.title: Logjam TLS downgrade protection
changes.canonicalSummary: coreTLS raised the minimum accepted ephemeral Diffie-Hellman key size for the documented export-cipher downgrade case.
changes.summary: Apple addressed CVE-2015-4000, known as Logjam, by increasing the default minimum ephemeral Diffie-Hellman key size from 512 to 768 bits.

changes.title: Mail HTML content replacement restriction
changes.canonicalSummary: Restricted HTML handling prevented a crafted email from replacing its visible message with an arbitrary webpage.
changes.summary: Apple addressed CVE-2015-3710 by limiting HTML email behavior that could refresh a viewed message with content from an arbitrary webpage.

events.summary: The public iOS 8.4.1 release repaired Apple Music library, playlist, artwork, Connect, and Beats 1 behavior while adding broad filesystem, network, account, code, media, and web security protections.

changes.title: iCloud Music Library and offline visibility fixes
changes.canonicalSummary: Users could enable iCloud Music Library and see added music when offline-only filtering had hidden it.
changes.summary: Apple repaired failures to turn on iCloud Music Library and a visibility issue caused by showing only music available offline.

changes.title: Playlist, artwork, Connect, and Beats 1 fixes
changes.canonicalSummary: The update improved new-playlist creation, album artwork consistency, artist posting, and the Beats 1 Love control.
changes.summary: Users gained a way to create a playlist when none existed, and Apple repaired cross-device artwork mismatches, several Connect posting problems, and Love taps in Beats 1.

citations.locator: iOS 8.4.1 — playlist, artwork, Connect, and Beats 1

changes.title: Filesystem path validation hardening
changes.canonicalSummary: AppleFileConduit, AirTraffic, and Backup received stronger validation for paths and symbolic links.
changes.summary: Apple addressed CVE-2015-5746, CVE-2015-5766, and CVE-2015-5752 by adding path checks, asset validation, and symlink sanitization around protected filesystem locations.

citations.locator: AppleFileConduit, Air Traffic, and Backup — CVE-2015-5746, CVE-2015-5766, and CVE-2015-5752

changes.title: Wi-Fi history broadcast minimization
changes.canonicalSummary: Network setup traffic stopped broadcasting identifiers for previously used Wi-Fi networks unrelated to the current SSID.
changes.summary: Apple addressed CVE-2015-3778 by limiting the MAC addresses broadcast during Wi-Fi connection setup to those associated with the current network name.

changes.title: Code-signing validation hardening
changes.canonicalSummary: Executable validation blocked several documented paths for appending or running unsigned code.
changes.summary: Apple strengthened validation for signed, multi-architecture, and Mach-O executables in fixes covering CVE-2015-3806, CVE-2015-3803, CVE-2015-3802, and CVE-2015-3805.
